    AI Overview
    The current USS Kearsarge (LHD-3) is an active Wasp-class amphibious assault ship commissioned in 1993, designed to deploy Marines, helicopters, and landing craft. Known for humanitarian efforts, including Hurricane Katrina relief, she conducted F-35B operations in early 2026. As of Feb 2026, she is active in the Atlantic. 
    Current Status and Known For (LHD-3): 
    • Mission: Known for amphibious assault, special operations, and humanitarian aid. 
    • Current Location: Recently active in the Atlantic Ocean conducting flight operations (as of Feb 2026). 
    • Key Capabilities: Carries MV-22 Ospreys, AH-64 Apache helicopters, and is capable of F-35B Lightning II landings. 
    • History Highlights: Rescued Capt. Scott O'Grady in 1995 and supported humanitarian efforts. 
    Deployment History (LHD-3): 
    • 1997: Evacuated non-combatants from Sierra Leone.
    • 2005: Provided disaster relief after Hurricane Katrina.
    • Recent Years: Regular deployments to the Middle East and the Mediterranean. 
    Other Ships Named Kearsarge: 
    • USS Kearsarge (1861): Famous Civil War sloop that sank the Confederate raider CSS Alabama in 1864.
    • USS Kearsarge (BB-5): Battleship known for its unique "double-stacked" turrets, later a crane ship.
    • USS Kearsarge (CV-33): Essex-class carrier that supported the Korean and Vietnam wars and served as a recovery ship for Mercury space missions. 
    See the Wikipedia page and US Carriers.Net for more detailed history, or follow the official Instagram for recent updates.

    What happened to the USS Kearsarge?
    Kearsarge was the recovery ship for the last two manned Project Mercury space missions in 1962–1963. She completed her career serving in the Vietnam War, earning five battle stars. She was decommissioned in 1970, and sold for scrap in 1974. The collection consists of 137 photos documenting the USS Kearsarge (CV-A33).

    USS Kearsarge (LHD-3) is the third Wasp-class amphibious assault ship of the United States Navy. She is the fifth ship to bear that name, but the fourth to serve under it, as the third was renamed Hornet before launching.
    Source: Wikipedia
     WikipediaMoreLessDescription
    Launched: March 26, 1992
    Length: 843′
    Construction started: February 6, 1990

    Builder: Ingalls Shipbuilding
    Draft: 26 ft 7 in (8.1 m)
    Size: 843 ft 2 in
